title: A chain theorem for planar PM-compact bricks
summary: A connected graph $G$ is matching covered if it contains at least one edge and every edge belongs to some perfect matching of $G$. A matching covered graph is a brick if it is 3-connected and after removing any two vertices, the resulting graph has a perfect matching. Bricks are the building blocks of matching covered graphs. A brick $G$ is extremal if the incidence vectors of all perfect matchings are linearly independent over $\mathbb{R}$. Zhou et al. [On planar extremal nonsolid bricks, J.
